co_present_vulns.name: pre-key-exchange message injection (server and client)
co_present_vulns.entry_point: raw socket peer injects a USERAUTH_REQUEST (toward the server) or an EXT_INFO (toward the client) in plaintext before kex completes
co_present_vulns.proof_present_at_C: exp_msg.py and exp_ext.py reproduce on a checkout of C: the targeted asyncssh endpoint accepts the early packet and stays up ('vulnerable'); after the fix it drops the connection ('blocked').

co_present_vulns.name: per-user authorized-keys path traversal via %u
co_present_vulns.entry_point: server configured with AuthorizedKeysFile '<base>/keys/%u/authorized_keys'; a client authenticates with username '../OUTSIDE' and a key planted outside the keys/ dir
co_present_vulns.proof_present_at_C: exp_authkeys.py: the traversing username authenticates an out-of-directory key on C ('vulnerable'); the legit per-user lookup still works; after the fix the username is rejected. IllegalUserName already exists in misc.py at C (no backport needed).

co_present_vulns.name: SCP client download path traversal
co_present_vulns.entry_point: asyncssh.scp((conn, path), dst) download from a server whose SCP source stream names a file '../escaped_evil'
co_present_vulns.proof_present_at_C: exp_scp.py: a file is written outside the destination directory on C ('vulnerable'); after the fix the name is rejected (SFTPBadMessage) and nothing escapes.

co_present_vulns.name: channel zero maximum-packet-size denial of service
co_present_vulns.entry_point: client opens a session advertising max_pktsize=0; the peer hangs when it has channel data to send
co_present_vulns.proof_present_at_C: _pktsize_scenario.py run under a wall-clock timeout: the endpoint hangs on C (killed by timeout = 'vulnerable'); after the fix it rejects the zero size during channel open with a ProtocolError and exits promptly.

verified.exploit_entry_point: All four are exercised through the real public transport over a loopback socket: the plaintext SSH handshake (raw-socket peer), per-user public-key authentication driven by server config, the scp() client download, and channel open. No internal helpers are called directly; no network is used.
variants: message injection, server direction: early USERAUTH_REQUEST before kex -> server must disconnect
message injection, client direction: early EXT_INFO before kex -> client must disconnect
authorized-keys traversal: username '../OUTSIDE' resolves the per-user %u template outside the key directory
SCP download traversal: C-record file name '../escaped_evil' writes above the destination directory
channel DoS: peer-advertised maximum packet size of 0 wedges the send path (distinct root cause and code path from the others)
message injection, server direction: early EXT_INFO before kex -> server must disconnect (2026-10-16)
message injection, client direction: early USERAUTH_SUCCESS before kex -> client must disconnect (2026-10-16)
SCP download traversal: absolute-path name and embedded 'sub/../../x' name (2026-10-16)
channel DoS: zero advertised by a peer with a dropbear version and compression (internal size -1) (2026-10-16)
channel DoS: zero advertised in the open confirmation, client is the target (2026-10-16)
message injection, mid-exchange window: plaintext USERAUTH_REQUEST and EXT_INFO toward the server after its NEWKEYS, before the client's NEWKEYS -> server must disconnect (2026-10-16)
message injection, mid-exchange window: plaintext EXT_INFO and USERAUTH_SUCCESS toward the client after its NEWKEYS, before the server's NEWKEYS -> client must disconnect (2026-10-16)
verified.project_tests_run: The verifier does not run /app's own tests (untrusted); it runs independent copies under /tests. Confirmed from source with pytest on CPython 3.9 (editable install of the vulnerable commit C): all 5 security tests FAIL on C (every exploit succeeds) and all 5 functional tests PASS; after the upstream source fix all 10 PASS, twice, in ~1.5s. The channel-DoS security test uses a 30s wall-clock subprocess timeout, so a vulnerable/incomplete fix is reported as a failure rather than hanging the verifier.

patch_checks.note: 2026-10-16 repair: reference fix with '== 0' instead of '<= 0'; a dropbear-version peer with compression turns an advertised 0 into -1 and still hangs
2026-10-16 repair: zero-size guard on incoming channel open only, not on the open confirmation
2026-10-16 repair: SCP name check rejects only a leading '../' (absolute and embedded traversal escape)
2026-10-16 repair: pre-kex guard only for the two reported packet types (USERAUTH_REQUEST to server, EXT_INFO to client)
2026-10-16 repair: user-name check rejects only '..' and a leading '../'

2026-10-16 repair (audit of DeepSeek r12): pre-kex guard keyed on the endpoint's own session id (set when it sends its own NEWKEYS), so a plaintext packet injected after the KEX reply and before the peer's NEWKEYS is still processed

notes: Pure Python, no services. python:3.11-slim base; asyncssh installed editable from the vulnerable commit C (NOT PyPI, which ships fixed releases). solution/fix.patch is the upstream source fix for all four vulns (config.py + connection.py + scp.py), source only. subset_fix drops the zero-packet-size guard (one security test fails, functional all pass). disable_feature over-restricts the SCP file-name check to reject any '.', which fixes the vulns but breaks legitimate downloads (functional fail). alt_correct_fix rewrites the three tractable guards (username, SCP name, packet size) in a different but correct form; the handshake state-machine change is kept as upstream since a hand-authored alternative there is not plausible to do safely.
